program_overview.title: Python and AI for Kids
program_overview.tagline: Real typed Python at 9 to 12: turtle art that wows, games with Pygame, and AI understood the kid-safe way, by training models, not chatting with bots.
program_overview.description:
Python is the friendliest real language a child can type, and this live online course makes the most of it for ages 9 to 12: from the first print statement to turtle graphics that draw spirals and snowflakes, real logic and loops, functions, files, first object-oriented thinking, and complete games built in Pygame that friends actually want to play.

The AI phase is deliberately kid-safe and hands-on: children learn what AI is by building it small, rules-based smart programs, data detective work on real (fun) datasets, and camera-based projects in the Teachable Machine style, where they train and test models themselves. There are no chatbot accounts and no AI-writes-the-code shortcuts, the major AI chat tools are 13+ by their own rules, and this course says so plainly while building the skills that will make such tools genuinely useful later.

The pace is honest and kid-sized: eight months at two live classes a week plus two to three hours of playful practice, with two more months in hand when needed. Homework after every class, a mixed challenge at the end of every month, and a final exam, a capstone demo plus a friendly viva, that decides the certificate, with a free retest after revision. Real Python, real games, real understanding.
what_makes_this_different: Real typed Python from day one, at a pace built for 9 to 12 year olds
Turtle graphics as the hook: art a child can print and stick on the fridge, powered by loops
Complete Pygame games: finished, playable, shared with family, not half-built demos
Kid-safe AI: models trained by the child, rules-based smart programs, no chatbot accounts (those tools are 13+, and we say so)
An honest 8-month arc with 2 months in hand: nobody is rushed, nobody coasts
Real assessment, gently done: monthly mixed challenges and a final capstone exam with a free retest

faqs.question: What will my child build in this Python course?
faqs.answer: More than 30 typed Python projects across eight months: joke machines and quiz games in the first weeks, turtle art worth printing, list-powered tools, save-file apps, complete Pygame games with scores and sounds, and in the AI phase a rules-based smart helper, data detective findings and a camera model the child trains personally. It all ends with a capstone presented at demo day.

faqs.question: What age is right for this course?
faqs.answer: Ages 9 to 12: old enough for real typing and abstract-enough thinking, young enough that the playful pace fits perfectly. Younger children thrive better in our Scratch-first Kids Coding course, which builds toward exactly this. Batches are grouped by age.

faqs.question: How long does it take a child to learn Python?
faqs.answer: Eight months at 2 live classes a week plus 2 to 3 hours of playful practice takes a child from first line to a demo-day capstone with games and a trained model behind them. The course keeps two more months in hand for children who need more repetition, no rushing, no penalty.

faqs.question: How is my child assessed? Is the certificate just for attending?
faqs.answer: No, and it is all gentle: classwork every session, a small build after every class, a monthly mixed challenge that revisits earlier skills so they stop fading, and a final exam, a capstone demo plus a friendly viva and short quiz. Passing earns the certificate; a child who falls short gets focused revision and a free retest.

faqs.question: How is AI taught to children this young?
faqs.answer: By building it small and honest. Children write rules-based smart programs in pure Python, do data detective work on fun datasets, and train camera models Teachable-Machine style with their own examples, then hunt for the model’s mistakes. There are no chatbot accounts: the major AI chat tools are 13+ by their own rules, and we say that plainly while building the skills that will make such tools truly useful later.

faqs.question: Python or Scratch first for my child?
faqs.answer: Scratch first for ages 6-8, Python from around 9 when typing and patience are ready. Children who arrive from Scratch fly here: the logic transfers instantly and the "real code" feeling is a powerful motivator. Our placement check settles it honestly either way.

faqs.question: Is any paid software needed?
faqs.answer: No. Python, the editor, Pygame and every tool used are free, and any reasonably recent computer runs them comfortably. No AI subscriptions exist in this course by design.

faqs.question: What are the fees?

A mini batch of 3-4 children is ₹2,999 per month, and personal 1-on-1 classes are ₹4,999 per month. International families pay a price set for their own country, shown on this page in their local currency.

faqs.question: Is there a free trial class?
faqs.answer: Yes, a free demo class with no commitment: book at learn.modernagecoders.com/contact or message us on WhatsApp at +91 91233 66161. Your child will write and run real Python inside the demo.

faqs.question: Are classes live or recorded?
faqs.answer: Live, always: small groups with a real teacher watching the child’s actual code, never pre-recorded videos. At this age the missing colon is the whole battle, and live eyes win it kindly.
